title: kv-prefix mixed-seqlen stress harness with burst-noise and regression hooks
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Purpose: build a deterministic, reproducible load harness that stresses the prefix/KV cache under realistic mixed sequence-length traffic and intermittent adversarial bursts. This ticket scopes a test harness that measures tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail behavior, and hit-rate vs memory trade-offs while injecting cold-start noise and eviction pressure. Goals: 1) produce a stable baseline metric (tokens/sec and p95) across repeated runs; 2) detect regressions automatically via statistical baselines and alerting hooks; 3) explore sensitivity to sequence-length mixture, burstiness, and memory fragmentation; 4) output artifacts (heatmaps, histogram diffs, time-series of occupancy/hitrate) for triage and perf calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end in CI and produces a reproducible run artifact (CSV + JSON summary) for a given seed
Metrics emitted: tokens_per_second (overall), p50/p95/p99 latency (token generation), cache_hit_rate (prefix-level), memory_usage_bytes, eviction_rate, synthetic_cold_start_fraction
Regression detector compares current run to stored baseline using bootstrap confidence intervals and flags a regression when p95 increases >10% with p<=0.01

Parameter sweep runner supports sequence-length distribution profiles (short/long/mixed), burst profiles (microburst, sustained spike), and memory caps; reports aggregated heatmaps of hit-rate vs p95 vs memory
CI job passes with smoke run and posts artifacts to S3 and a Grafana link; on regression trigger posts Slack alert to #perf-regressions with summary and links to artifacts
